purpose: Expose the accepted Center & Scheduling administration capabilities through one protected own-center browser surface without moving authorization or persistence into route code.
success_outcome: An authenticated Admin can manage own-center classes, recurring schedules, teacher invitations, assignments, and revocation in the browser, while server-owned scope prevents privilege escalation and removed Teachers immediately lose assigned-class authority.
anti_goals: Do not add user-selected roles, Admin promotion, passwords, development login, or another center bootstrap mechanism.
Do not trust submitted center, role, account, assignment, or Admin authority fields.
Do not move Center & Scheduling or Identity & Access persistence into SvelteKit routes.

stop_conditions: Stop if the Admin surface requires client-owned authorization, direct route persistence, Teacher-to-Admin promotion, or a new ownership edge outside the accepted Center & Scheduling and Identity & Access boundaries.

constraints: Every Admin read and command resolves the actor and own-center scope on the server and delegates persistence to the accepted owner boundary.
Teacher invitations may create only permitted participant roles; no browser field can promote a Teacher to Admin or widen center scope.
Assignment and membership removal take effect at the next owner-boundary authorization check.
invariants: Class, schedule, participant, and assignment state remains center-bounded and is written only by its owning capability.
A Teacher can access or change only assigned classes and immediately loses that authority after assignment or membership removal.
An individual class never accepts more than one student.
verification_targets: FT-002-AC-007 / REQ-003 / REQ-004: protected browser/HTTP flow for own-center class CRUD, individual/group capacity, recurring schedule creation, teacher invitation, assignment, and removal.
FT-002-AC-007 / REQ-014: negative matrix for unauthenticated, non-Admin, cross-center, forged-scope, invalid-role, and post-revocation operations with unchanged unauthorized state.
